did_you_know.text: Did you know? This verse describes someone who seeks to isolate himself in order to pursue his own desires, presenting such withdrawal as contrary to wisdom and sound judgment.
Did you know? A person’s words are compared to deep waters, while his wisdom is compared to a flowing spring—images expressing depth and abundance.
Did you know? The verse compares a person who is slack in his work to one who destroys, presenting negligence at work as part of destructive behavior.
Did you know? The name of the LORD is described as a strong tower: the righteous run to it and are safe, finding security and protection in him.
Did you know? The verse contrasts pride before destruction with humility before honor, linking a person’s attitude to the consequences of his path.
Did you know? Proverbs warns against giving an answer before hearing the matter, calling it folly and shame.
Did you know? Even when the first person in a dispute seems right, the verse reminds us to hear the other side and examine the matter before reaching a decision.
Did you know? The verse presents casting lots as a way to settle disputes and separate strong opponents.
Did you know? The tongue is described as having the power of life and death, and a person will eat the fruit of his words—that is, bear the consequences of what he says.
Did you know? The verse distinguishes between having many companions and having a loyal, devoted friend: the faithfulness of one friend may be deeper than the bond of a brother.
